episodes.152378: During the early morning hours of October 21st, a series of training thunderstorms brought heavy rain to portions of central Indiana.  The heaviest rain fell across an axis generally just north of I-70 with rain amounts in excess of 3 inches in spots.  This lead to a few areas of minor flooding with little impacts noted.
episodes.152593: Strong onshore winds and deep moisture resulted in numerous showers and embedded thunderstorms over the Atlantic during the early morning hours. Several thunderstorms moved onshore and produced strong convective wind gusts.
episodes.152687: A nearby front and upper air troughs generated periods of heavy rain across Oahu and Kauai. The precipitation caused ponding on roadways, and small stream and drainage ditch flooding. No serious injuries or property damage were reported.
episodes.152719: Surface trough draped to the west of South Florida and lingering moisture in it's wake helped to spark convection across the east coast of South Florida and adjacent Atlantic and Biscayne Bay waters. Furthermore, brisk easterly flow aided a few storms to produce some strong wind gusts.
episodes.152962: On the morning of October 21st a warm front stalled over northern Ohio. This feature brought repeating showers and thunderstorms to the City of Cleveland and surrounding areas. Following a recent wet period, the ground was near saturation and smaller community storm drainage systems were near capacity. Moderate rainfall measuring over an inch an hour. Several road closers and a few water rescues resulted from area flooding.
episodes.153041: Surface trough draped to the west of South Florida, combined with swath of deep tropical moisture across the region helped to spark convection across the east coast of South Florida. Repeated rounds of heavy rainfall produced flooding across Broward.
episodes.153819: Occasional gale-force wind gusts in occurred with frequent rain and thunderstorm squalls throughout the Florida Keys coastal waters as a slow-moving tropical wave amplified over the western Caribbean Sea.  The squalls occurred over a period from the afternoon of October 18th through the evening of October 20th.

events.narrative: Between 4 and 7 AM rainfall amounts between 2 and 2.5 inches fell across the City of Cleveland and much of Cuyahoga County. This disrupted morning commutes with widespread road closures.  Cars were stuck in high water on Jennings Road in Cleveland. Roads that were closured due to flooding include; I-90 EB closed to Innerbelt and I-71/Jennings SB, MLK Jr. Dr. SB just south of I-90, MLK Jr. Dr. SB between East Blvd & Liberty Rd, I-90 at W 44th St., I-90 West at Mckinley Ave, W. 150 closed just north of I-480, I-90 WB at Mckinley, W. 117th at Madison Avenue, Pepper Pike Gates Mill Blvd, and Coit and E. 131st St.
